short: The lead ship of the Royal Navy's light aircraft carriers, instrumental in the Falklands War.
full:
Commissioned on 11 July 1980, HMS Invincible (R05) was the lead ship of her class of light aircraft carriers. Originally conceived as a "through-deck cruiser" to command anti-submarine task groups, it was equipped with the Sea Harrier aircraft, which revolutionised naval aviation with short take-off and vertical landing capabilities. In 1982, Invincible formed the core of the British task force dispatched to reclaim the Falkland Islands alongside HMS Hermes.

The carrier's performance during the Falklands War vindicated the concept of the modern light carrier and the Sea Harrier, proving crucial to establishing local air superiority in the South Atlantic. It subsequently participated in operations over the Balkans and Iraq, maintaining Britain's ability to project air power from the sea. After twenty-five years of service, Invincible was decommissioned on 3 August 2005.
